### Why "Sweating It Out" Doesn't Work

- **No faster detox:** Exercise or a sauna will not speed up how fast your body clears alcohol or acetaldehyde (a byproduct that drives hangover symptoms).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXX96_44Drxwjrn-4LxWLzzA7kp_smdNeJI9pmDg_nPSz1wfxvHdJP51EDli6rlYFRBahlCawRBAXoWKJhMW2sC_OpRc6sxYULl7vc5fuSvfsO0ir55vQuf3cqMPChBYcN2_VxP3_-Yr9mRRZazeDEJOUY5Tw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnAEBxCJF1yZ-UcYZLzIKYpD4s8ykVzF-EglctINcsoezpcuP1Xg7WWdStAnF7ANii_0JakUpXszXMTIysYgQ3RDlL9i8q-PHSozC9RS2Ne3NRsIz0DPEUhnyRqpCvWI5bMni8EDOFqVZmdlc6oujrdrvZxr26_XCFvCbxb-WmG4jd1v06XgtPzgXDrm4Kd4nC_6EIEl25f7oYgcEv28)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmQEBxCJF19r4Je-BDjvNTBmeQ7FzufIgaCwYZMsiYwLqrEyOe6S0BLifUYVdcd_d-pkH9bS1_sBh0eLds1U0XcuEd0qE9-Y49KWEISYrso92V11b1HttNuf9o1kjabukePJa5SXQipAAppDPbDBz0CVzjhwUT-yfFxRgLb4A3W-4Rb4sNLxAZ1GRYMpSuEe4TsdElEaNY1iCmOY)
- **Worse dehydration:** Alcohol acts as a diuretic. Sweating heavily drains even more fluids and electrolytes, which can make headaches, fatigue, and dizziness worse.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXC31k6p0qyMD8dVOPXBaCDohlJN4eN7YwAwwu5ZsAgbpXWjmijnZmqwULAwr_N-Shqx6Pd_Yxj-9GdO96gLLcUFpA3ukEvdmaXfoqYWntKRAY83J5JDmuLF8CK75UHuaYS7nIQAza)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESzQEBxCJF1yPSMUKwPfzsYLVeZY3R5kVCgV8mgN6fntIGF9eOnMjuK8FpPX69CP9Dd1fNT6jhCqcv8unqbG1V0HWi3xwx3-xvE4hH3Sz6d5SCipMZF12gadZBW_Mdu2gIhoxsfSv8l7JMe7BBoH5uSi-qC8ifvkPG41qRmCsw56nqt9zKS90cu9eGEk8XrYKUetU4g3VM2_deadTVXc8oTTHNZIetr4lqqfzVEyhlFnwVuswMglKf6JuxPCyqAA1ZFtF-qORFohxtGAUuNrpc)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXXfiTi6MuDDcc8HKGctL-I6XRUuRqlVX2UIFdAZSwXbd1cwxTvnf4-h_Wcf2sLE5IcJetK7d_AlgpjN5l35soK5JVqc8ozR8-N12tRWyU1ji9ce6EC-J_QsyyQM4hfypxJ7A)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXrRoBhK0e_gjCyE0ydxPTQTSSRJsD1jdpE7gK68N-cKmTP4_LFg5QiZ0nCtste1HZCIEfXfv5dFwfGcPebVLYD8VUdrCXH5Qh_oVjPbAJ7_ujFswekLMyK2dwB--apH6JSnrwfRtky-9JynT-GT_LeqMlxg)
- **Extra physical strain:** Poor sleep, low blood sugar, and reduced coordination raise your risk of injury or heart strain during hard workouts.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXXvrnM09kZsaezu2y4pgB8vUjr9nG0dLt5g3e4la4sfFEeoZIYFcOUvKCf0PLIchV79VRs0h8to85OES0O3h8t8yHLTkcNwBDiTa4ihHyBwAvSrBdyqlcMrdAy-Amqn23cvVfg1dqFzS0HXBcqWJbtcdj7h2hEw0wx)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXX96_44Drxwjrn-4LxWLzzA7kp_smdNeJI9pmDg_nPSz1wfxvHdJP51EDli6rlYFRBahlCawRBAXoWKJhMW2sC_OpRc6sxYULl7vc5fuSvfsO0ir55vQuf3cqMPChBYcN2_VxP3_-Yr9mRRZazeDEJOUY5Tw)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlQEBxCJF1-ZDGZqsFlfVJz0-AZt1Z-fyN6xSFz27Rk9B3cGaXBlfyyTbavlwV7A3TQer64SyTMl80Z0x1q8ZfFWbjZavQ3NuGuEO4ntibYR6oymKf0e8A5ZWR8BfiDWkKRs6Z0DjEf65qyvTIH9n-7cGTA-r-agNHSKJX4Pkf5HQqOJxta_rD-kAn8F1gHQT_qIXQmXIvw)

### Why Some People Feel Better After Moving

As explained in [The Guardian](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnAEBxCJF1yZ-UcYZLzIKYpD4s8ykVzF-EglctINcsoezpcuP1Xg7WWdStAnF7ANii_0JakUpXszXMTIysYgQ3RDlL9i8q-PHSozC9RS2Ne3NRsIz0DPEUhnyRqpCvWI5bMni8EDOFqVZmdlc6oujrdrvZxr26_XCFvCbxb-WmG4jd1v06XgtPzgXDrm4Kd4nC_6EIEl25f7oYgcEv28) , workouts or saunas can temporarily ease how you feel by releasing endorphins, lowering stress hormones, and improving circulation—not by removing toxins . Similarly, [HealthHP](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXXvrnM09kZsaezu2y4pgB8vUjr9nG0dLt5g3e4la4sfFEeoZIYFcOUvKCf0PLIchV79VRs0h8to85OES0O3h8t8yHLTkcNwBDiTa4ihHyBwAvSrBdyqlcMrdAy-Amqn23cvVfg1dqFzS0HXBcqWJbtcdj7h2hEw0wx) notes that endorphins and increased alertness can mask symptoms, though intense effort carries risks when dehydrated or fatigued. Opinions on [Reddit](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnAEBxCJF14qR3JBFeC0uDgHF-dfuL6Yxh-isf9w9eISf5IchawYsZDG29dbwhiC4bTVraLAPeHVzOBbopu9Aq4dCGX1US6j7v1ILCST3nch5Ba_ohRe3kbNtKJG2vjefsjJhS5hnQuRuF49zIxmFnDyODuwyezElt6Dzou5pm7xe_M3-cN9skjV1DL9QvQ1XtvsH9J8hrPUoG_oAqp4) are mixed: while some users say light exercise or sweating helps them feel better, many note that dehydration makes it counterproductive.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnAEBxCJF1yZ-UcYZLzIKYpD4s8ykVzF-EglctINcsoezpcuP1Xg7WWdStAnF7ANii_0JakUpXszXMTIysYgQ3RDlL9i8q-PHSozC9RS2Ne3NRsIz0DPEUhnyRqpCvWI5bMni8EDOFqVZmdlc6oujrdrvZxr26_XCFvCbxb-WmG4jd1v06XgtPzgXDrm4Kd4nC_6EIEl25f7oYgcEv28)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXXvrnM09kZsaezu2y4pgB8vUjr9nG0dLt5g3e4la4sfFEeoZIYFcOUvKCf0PLIchV79VRs0h8to85OES0O3h8t8yHLTkcNwBDiTa4ihHyBwAvSrBdyqlcMrdAy-Amqn23cvVfg1dqFzS0HXBcqWJbtcdj7h2hEw0wx)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnAEBxCJF14qR3JBFeC0uDgHF-dfuL6Yxh-isf9w9eISf5IchawYsZDG29dbwhiC4bTVraLAPeHVzOBbopu9Aq4dCGX1US6j7v1ILCST3nch5Ba_ohRe3kbNtKJG2vjefsjJhS5hnQuRuF49zIxmFnDyODuwyezElt6Dzou5pm7xe_M3-cN9skjV1DL9QvQ1XtvsH9J8hrPUoG_oAqp4)

### What Actually Helps

- **Rehydrate:** Drink water and replenish electrolytes.
- **Rest and eat:** Get sleep and eat bland, balanced foods to steady blood sugar.
- **Keep movement light:** If symptoms are mild and you are hydrated, a short walk or gentle stretching is safer than intense exercise. Skip workouts and seek medical care if you have severe symptoms like persistent vomiting, chest pain, confusion, or a racing/irregular heartbeat.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlQEBxCJF1-ZDGZqsFlfVJz0-AZt1Z-fyN6xSFz27Rk9B3cGaXBlfyyTbavlwV7A3TQer64SyTMl80Z0x1q8ZfFWbjZavQ3NuGuEO4ntibYR6oymKf0e8A5ZWR8BfiDWkKRs6Z0DjEf65qyvTIH9n-7cGTA-r-agNHSKJX4Pkf5HQqOJxta_rD-kAn8F1gHQT_qIXQmXIvw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXXWXWHvMvGh_zhf4tMt9u-08VgqMDs0s7Nfzlz2sutIOPSNovlb9XVDWaLfMFx3geIrDYVtA62oWrhZdDq3ZxHhVDvCJLrPJXs9wE_c5nJbeaydsufr4ZtTuxkaIQfuLMU)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXX96_44Drxwjrn-4LxWLzzA7kp_smdNeJI9pmDg_nPSz1wfxvHdJP51EDli6rlYFRBahlCawRBAXoWKJhMW2sC_OpRc6sxYULl7vc5fuSvfsO0ir55vQuf3cqMPChBYcN2_VxP3_-Yr9mRRZazeDEJOUY5Tw)

items.title: What Actually Helps
items.text: Rehydrate: Drink water and replenish electrolytes. Rest and eat: Get sleep and eat bland, balanced foods to steady blood sugar. Keep movement light: If symptoms are mild and you are hydrated, a short walk or gentle stretching is safer than intense exercise. Skip workouts and seek medical care if you have severe symptoms like persistent vomiting, chest pain, confusion, or a racing/irregular heartbeat.
